pure-announcement.rationale: It is vendor content marketing making a framework argument, not a launch, release note, or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts cover SIEM event visibility and MCP server governance; neither states this note's data-governance framework of agent identity lifecycle, query-level ABAC enforcement, decision-provenance audit, and lineage.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Its statistics are of mixed quality but consistently sourced (McKinsey, MIT NANDA, arxiv, Microsoft maturity model, EU AI Act text), so a reader can trace and check the claims.

durability.rationale: The piece is explicitly year-stamped ('playbook for 2026') and load-bearing on perishable adoption statistics (30% at maturity level 3, 51% in production, 40% canceled by 2027) and current regulation dates, even though the underlying agents-as-principals framework would age better.

actionability.rationale: It prescribes concrete, vendor-independent controls — an agent registry, per-agent service accounts, explicit offboarding, machine-executable policies like the DENY-bulk-SELECT example, structured audit fields including the reasoning trace, and governance metrics such as false-positive rate.

atomicity.rationale: It bundles the breaks-for-agents argument, a failure-statistics survey, the four-component framework, a regulatory tour, and a CDO operating model — several separable strands rather than one paragraph-stateable core.
